_comment: Editable settings for the BI Dev Assistant. Restart the app after changing this file.
_note_on_focus_mode: Focus mode is intentionally NOT in this list. Power BI Desktop has no dedicated JSON property for it - it's simply the enabled default, and PBI only ever writes properties that differ from default. So it's never written by this tool either; every icon listed below gets explicitly disabled instead, which leaves Focus mode as the only one still on.
_note_on_color_palette: Source of truth: the 'Power BI Sequence' sheet in WTW_Data_Visualization_Color_Catalog.xlsx, in this exact order (order matters for the report theme's dataColors array). This checks VISUAL/data colors only - color_object_allowlist deliberately excludes text, label, axis, legend, title and gridline properties.
_note_on_color_object_allowlist: Deliberately excludes 'fill' - on chart-type visuals it's not used, and on UI elements (buttons, shapes, page navigators) it's chrome/branding, not a data color, so including it just produced noise (e.g. flagging a deliberately-branded button color as a 'data color' violation).
_note_on_export_compliant_values: report.json's settings.exportDataMode value(s) that count as compliant (not a violation). 'None' (export fully disabled) is confirmed directly from real project data. 'AllowSummarized' (summarized-data-only export) is the best-evidenced name for the other state you said should also be acceptable, but Microsoft doesn't publish an authoritative enum list for this property - if your projects use a different exact string for 'summarized only', add it here. The auto-fix always sets exportDataMode to 'None' (the one unambiguous, always-safe value), regardless of which of these was missing.
_note_on_tcto_path_prefixes: The approved TCTO SharePoint location every table's data source is expected to resolve to. Confirmed directly from the real DC & Benefit Affordability Dashboard's expressions.tmdl (its 'SourceFile' shared parameter). A source resolving to a path that doesn't start with one of these prefixes is flagged for review; add another entry here for a different project's own approved TCTO subfolder.
_note_on_alignment_excluded_page_substri: Rule 10 (table/matrix alignment) is skipped entirely on any page whose display name contains one of these substrings (case-insensitive). Confirmed against a real page, 'Info (Plan design)', whose Matrix is a flat glossary list with no Values well at all - it has no 'Specific column' override in the Format pane to fix at all, only a 'Row headers > Alignment' control this tool doesn't yet know how to write safely. Add another entry here for a different project's own equivalent page-naming convention.
